instruction.text: Drag the mud to the wooden poles.

atoms.b: Most buildings in Anglo-Saxon ((++villages pillages)) were made with a technique called wattle and daub. This involved putting wooden ((++poles holes)) into the ground and then covering them in clay and mud.
However, Anglo-Saxons did build some things from stone. For example, this is an Anglo-Saxon ((++church market)) in St Albans.
atoms.sound: However, Anglo-Saxons did build some things from stone. For example, this is an Anglo-Saxon church in St Awlbans.

instruction.text: Can you find the river on the map?

feedback.end: Anglo-Saxons normally built their settlements very close to water because it was so useful.

instruction.text: What do you think Anglo-Saxons used rivers for? Select the three correct answers.

feedback.finish: Anglo-Saxons travelled in boats on rivers and had watermills to grind flour. They also used the water for drinking, cooking and washing.

instruction.text: Select the correct type of house to learn more about Anglo-Saxon settlements.

feedback.end: Most villagers’ houses were small and only had one room. The village also had a wall around it. This protected the animals from predators and the people from rival tribes.
The chief’s house was much bigger than the other houses because it was also used as a banqueting hall to entertain guests.

instruction.text: How do you think we know what Anglo-Saxon villages looked like?

feedback.end: Archaeologists have excavated Anglo-Saxon villages; meaning they have dug up their remains. From these excavations, we can work out how Anglo-Saxons likely lived.

instruction.text: Read the text and answer the questions.

hint.label: Fertile
hint.text: Fertile means the soil has lots of nutrients, and it is easy to grow plants.

atoms.text: Anglo-Saxon life revolved around farming. Land in Britain was much more fertile and less likely to flood than the flat land in Northern Europe. This meant that they could farm much more easily in Britain.

atoms.a: What did Anglo-Saxon life revolve around?
What was better in Britain than in Northern Europe?
